Recode a latent variable into a Likert response

Source: R/draw_categorical.R
draw_likert.Rd

A convenience wrapper around draw_ordered that constructs equally spaced breaks between min and max.

Usage

draw_likert(
  x,
  min = NULL,
  max = NULL,
  bins = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Latent numeric variable.

min, max

Range the latent variable is cut on, rather than a filter applied to it: a value outside [min, max] joins the outermost bin. For 1.0.2's behaviour, where such a value became NA, call draw_ordered(x, breaks = seq(min, max, length.out = bins + 1), strict = TRUE).

bins

Number of Likert categories.

breaks

Manual interior cut-points, read as draw_ordered() reads them, so length(breaks) + 1 categories. An alternative to min, max, and bins. 1.0.2 read the same vector as the full set of bin boundaries; the strict = TRUE call above returns that answer.

labels

Optional category labels.

Value

An integer vector of category indices, one per element of x, or an ordered factor with those labels when they are supplied.

Examples

fabricate(N = 100, x = rnorm(N),
          likert = draw_likert(x, min = -3, max = 3, bins = 5))
#> # A tibble: 100 × 3
#>    ID         x likert
#>    <chr>  <dbl>  <int>
#>  1 001    0.347      3
#>  2 002   -0.918      2
#>  3 003    1.34       4
#>  4 004   -1.08       2
#>  5 005    1.07       4
#>  6 006    0.529      3
#>  7 007   -1.66       2
#>  8 008    0.678      4
#>  9 009   -1.07       2
#> 10 010   -0.341      3
#> # ℹ 90 more rows
